verdict.rationale: Microsoft Graph documents change notifications that alert applications when an Outlook resource they care about is created, updated, or deleted. It also offers rich notifications that carry the changed resource's data, so first-party event subscription exists. However, the pack never shows that these alerts are delivered as registrable outbound HTTP callbacks to an endpoint the consumer controls. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of HTTP webhook endpoint registration (subscription creation, notification URL, validation), subscription lifecycle/renewal details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Change notifications enable applications to receive alerts when a Microsoft Graph resource they're interested in changes; that is, created, updated, or deleted.
Change notifications that include the resource data of the object that changed.
